"Recent indicators suggest that economic activity expanded at a strong pace in the third quarter." In a policy context, the Taylor rule (Taylor, 1993) and estimates in Clarida, Galí, and Gertler (1999) imply that stronger activity (a positive output gap) alongside elevated inflation points to a tighter or sustained restrictive stance, while the short-run Phillips curve trade-off suggests upward pressure on inflation; thus the tone is growth-positive but mildly hawkish for policy.
